title: Copenhagen Climate Ministerial 2026 Sets Electrification as Core COP31 Priority Ahead of Antalya
detail: The fifth Copenhagen Climate Ministerial convened on May 20–21, 2026, with climate ministers from major economies setting priorities for COP31 in Antalya, Türkiye (November 2026). Turkish COP31 Presidency head Murat Kurum called for dramatically expanding electrification across all sectors of the economy. IRENA presented a global goal to increase electricity's share of final energy to 35% by 2035 — up from approximately 22% today. Australia and EU officials agreed to work on a new joint global electrification initiative. IPCC Chair Jim Skea delivered a state-of-the-climate address. Key outcomes include agreement to make electrification the cornerstone of COP31 deliverables and to strengthen the Global Stocktake's electrification tracking mechanisms.

media.caption: Copenhagen Climate Ministerial 2026 — global climate ministers align on electrification as COP31 centerpiece

title: 30 MW Barrow Green Hydrogen Project Reaches FID — Plug Power Electrolyzers to Cut Kimberly-Clark Emissions 50%
detail: The 30 MW Barrow Green Hydrogen Project in Barrow-in-Furness, Cumbria (UK) achieved final investment decision, with Plug Power supplying six 5 MW GenEco PEM electrolyzers. Operated by a Schroders Greencoat / Carlton Power partnership, the facility will use renewable electricity to produce approximately 100 GWh per year of green hydrogen for Kimberly-Clark's nearby manufacturing site (maker of Andrex and Kleenex brands), cutting the site's natural gas consumption by up to 50% and reducing CO2 emissions by 18,300 tonnes per year. The project demonstrates the industrial decarbonization use case for green hydrogen in hard-to-electrify manufacturing processes, one of the key applications highlighted in net-zero scenarios from the IEA and IPCC.

media.caption: 30 MW Barrow green hydrogen project reaches FID — Plug Power electrolyzers will cut Kimberly-Clark factory emissions by 50%
